title: Design System: Syed Junaid Khalander — Portfolio

ink-navy.displayName: Ink Navy (light theme text / dark theme button text)

display.purpose: Section h1 titles only, one per section.

label.purpose: Skill/project tag pills and nav links.

motion.name: reveal-ease
motion.purpose: Section fade-up on scroll into view, 600ms.

motion.name: interaction-ease
motion.purpose: Hover/focus transitions on links, buttons, theme toggle, 300ms.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: High-contrast inverted fill; used for the main CTA and every project 'View code' link.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font-weight: 600; padding: 1rem 1.25rem; border-radius: 2rem; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.14); box-shadow: 0 10px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.25); background: #f8fafc; color: #0f172a; cursor: pointer; transition: all 300ms ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(1.05); transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #f5b971; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: The only place the secondary hue (Alert Red) appears; used solely for 'View Resume'.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { font-weight: 600; padding: 1rem 1.25rem; border-radius: 2rem; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.14); box-shadow: 0 10px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.25); background: #ef4444; color: #ffffff; cursor: pointer; transition: all 300ms ease; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { filter: brightness(1.05); transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #f5b971; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Chip
components.description: Static informational tag; skills and project tech tags. No selected/active state.
components.css: .ds-chip { border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.14); background: rgba(255,255,255,0.03); color: #f8fafc; border-radius: 999px; padding: 0.45rem 0.75rem; font-size: 0.92rem; }

components.name: Card
components.description: The primary content container: genuinely frosted glass (backdrop-filter blur) over the gradient field, center-aligned.
components.html:
Current Focus

Engineering student focused on building usable software, smart systems, and project-based solutions.
components.css: .ds-card { padding: 1.5rem; background: rgba(15,19,31,0.7); backdrop-filter: blur(20px) saturate(160%); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(20px) saturate(160%); border-radius: 2rem; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.14); text-align: center; box-shadow: 0 16px 36px rgba(0,0,0,0.25); } .ds-card h3 { margin-bottom: 0.5rem; color: #f8fafc; } .ds-card p { color: #c5cedd; line-height: 1.6; }

components.name: Theme Toggle
components.description: Signature control present in both desktop and mobile nav; label swaps ☾ Dark / ☀ Light.
components.css: .ds-theme-toggle { border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.14); background: rgba(15,19,31,0.92); color: #f8fafc; border-radius: 999px; padding: 0.7rem 1rem; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.95rem; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: 0 12px 30px rgba(0,0,0,0.25); transition: all 300ms ease; } .ds-theme-toggle:hover { border-color: #f5b971; color: #f5b971; transform: translateY(-1px); }

narrative.overview: The portfolio reads as an engineering instrument panel at night: a near-black navy field, lit by a single warm amber signal, housed in soft translucent glass panels. It is warm and approachable rather than clinical — the amber glow and rounded, pill-shaped controls keep the "console" from feeling sterile or corporate, while the restraint of the accent color keeps it precise rather than decorative. The system exists in full light-mode parity (near-white "paper" field, rust/burnt-orange signal), toggled by the visitor and persisted locally, so every token below has a confirmed pair in both themes.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first radial-gradient field (near-black navy) with a full light-theme pair, switched via [data-theme] and persisted in localStorage.
One warm accent color (amber in dark, rust/burnt-orange in light), used sparingly — hover states, links, and small labels only, never as a fill.
Translucent "glass" panel surfaces (rgba backgrounds) layered over the gradient field instead of opaque cards.
Heavily rounded, near-pill geometry everywhere — buttons, chips, nav toggle, cards.
Soft, diffuse ambient shadows; no hard/crisp drop shadows.
Tactile hover language: small upward lift (translateY(-1px)) plus a brightness bump, never a scale-pop.

rules.name: The Rare Amber Rule
rules.body: The accent color never fills a surface. It appears only on link hover/underline, the scroll-progress bar, card-meta labels, certificate sub-titles, focus-visible outlines, and hover states of the scroll-to-top button and theme toggle.

rules.name: The Matched-Pair Rule
rules.body: No color token exists in only one theme. Every dark-theme token has a confirmed light-theme counterpart with the same role.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Every weight and size on the page comes from Poppins. Do not introduce a second family for emphasis — use size, weight, or the rare accent color instead.

rules.name: The Glass-Console Rule
rules.body: Depth comes from translucency and blur (backdrop-filter: blur(20px) saturate(160%)) over the gradient field, not from stacking opaque cards. Small persistent controls that must stay legible over busy content (scroll-to-top, theme toggle) stay fully opaque instead.

rules.name: The No-Hard-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow is large-blur and low-opacity. A tight, dark, high-contrast shadow is off-system on sight.

dos: Do keep the accent color rare — hover states, small labels, the progress bar. Never a background fill.
Do build every new surface as translucent glass over the gradient field before reaching for an opaque card.
Do use large-blur, low-opacity shadows only.
Do round generously — 2rem for panels/cards, 999px for pills/chips/toggles.
Do design every new color token as a matched dark/light pair before shipping either half.
Do keep hover feedback to a small lift (translateY(-1px)) plus a brightness bump.
donts: Don't add crisp, high-contrast, or colored shadows.
Don't use the secondary hue (Alert Red / Ember Orange) anywhere but the 'View Resume' CTA.
